title: The galvanic cell: making electrons take the wire

concepts.label: half-cell
concepts.definition: One half-reaction in its own container: a metal electrode in contact with a solution of its own ions.

concepts.label: electrode
concepts.definition: The solid conductor (here a metal strip) of a half-cell, where electrons enter or leave the solid.

concepts.label: anode (oxidation)
concepts.definition: The electrode where oxidation happens; electrons leave the cell from it; the negative (−) terminal of a galvanic cell.

concepts.label: cathode (reduction)
concepts.definition: The electrode where reduction happens; electrons arrive at it; the positive (+) terminal of a galvanic cell.

concepts.label: salt bridge / separator
concepts.definition: An ion path between the two half-cells (a tube of inert salt solution such as KNO3, or a porous wall) that keeps both solutions neutral without letting them mix; without it charge builds up and the current stops.

concepts.label: galvanic (voltaic) cell
concepts.definition: A device that turns a spontaneous redox reaction into electric current by separating the half-reactions so that electrons must travel through an external wire while ions close the loop inside.

concepts.label: Daniell cell
concepts.definition: The galvanic cell Zn | Zn2+ || Cu2+ | Cu (zinc in zinc sulfate, copper in copper sulfate; Daniell, 1836), about 1.10 V with 1 mol/L solutions.

concepts.label: voltage (push)
concepts.definition: Qualitative: how hard a cell pushes each electron from anode to cathode, in volts; set by the pair of half-cells (bigger the further apart the metals are in the activity series).

concepts.label: current (flow)
concepts.definition: Qualitative: how many electrons pass through the wire per second; depends on the voltage and on how easy the external path is.

concepts.label: cell notation
concepts.definition: One-line description of a cell, anode on the left: anode | anode solution || cathode solution | cathode, with | a phase boundary and || the salt bridge.

namedOnly: volt (unit used, defined in Charge, energy and capacity)
voltmeter (instrument that reads the push while passing almost no current)
short circuit (a thick wire as the external path)
Nernst equation / voltage sag as ions run out (pointer only)
state symbols (s), (aq) in the fuller cell notation
voltages add along the series (Zn–Fe + Fe–Cu = Zn–Cu), as a teaser for electrode potentials
summary: Running example: the zinc strip in copper sulfate from the redox lesson, pulled apart into the Daniell cell Zn | Zn2+ || Cu2+ | Cu; drawn with one dot = 0.025 mol of ions, 150 mL of 1 mol/L per half-cell, a KNO3 salt bridge, and measured voltages for Zn–Cu 1.10 V, Fe–Cu 0.78 V, Zn–Fe 0.32 V, Cu–Ag 0.46 V, Zn–Ag 1.56 V (from Chem.E0). Capstone: an animated cell whose metals (Zn, Fe, Cu, Ag), wire (open / bulb / short circuit) and salt bridge can be changed while electrode masses, electrons transferred and ion counts update. Later lessons can reuse: anode = oxidation = (−) in a galvanic cell, electrons anode → cathode in the wire, anions drift to the anode side and cations to the cathode side, charge build-up without an ion path, 'voltage = push, current = flow', and the fact that gaps along the series add.
